key_insight: PhysAssistBench shows that medical LLMs need to coordinate clinical knowledge, patient dialogue, and EHR tool use in the same interaction—not just excel at each separately.
clinical_relevance: This benchmark suggests current LLMs are not yet reliable for assisting physicians in real-world workflows where requests are underspecified, patient language is ambiguous, and EHR actions require precision.
method: Built from real MIMIC-IV cases into interactive doctor-patient-EHR scenarios
Uses agentic patient simulations that preserve record-grounded clinical facts across multi-turn exchanges
Includes a curated bilingual set of 1,296 manually reviewed and physician-validated turns
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experiments with leading LLMs, and they remained unreliable on PhysAssistBench despite the benchmark’s physician-validated evaluation set.
watch_item: Because the benchmark relies on simulated interactive patients from retrospective EHR data, performance on this task may not fully capture the complexity and safety demands of live clinical use.
paper_title: Are LLMs Ready to Assist Physicians? PhysAssistBench for Interactive Doctor-Patient-EHR Assistance
